questions.question: Which newspaper does Clark Kent work for?
questions.fact: In Superman's earliest stories the paper was called the Daily Star. It became the Daily Planet around 1940.

questions.question: What is Superman's Kryptonian birth name?
questions.fact: His Kryptonian father, Jor-El, was played by Marlon Brando in the 1978 film "Superman".

questions.question: Who played Superman in the 1978 film "Superman"?
questions.fact: The film's famous tagline promised audiences: "You'll believe a man can fly."

questions.question: Who is Superman's bald arch-enemy?
questions.fact: In his very first comic appearances, in 1940, Lex Luthor actually had a full head of red hair.

questions.question: In which year did Superman first appear in a comic?
questions.fact: A copy of his debut comic, Action Comics #1, reportedly sold for 6 million dollars at auction in 2024.

questions.question: What is Wonder Woman's everyday name?
questions.fact: Her creator, psychologist William Moulton Marston, also worked on an early lie detector. Fitting for her Lasso of Truth.

questions.question: What is the name of Wonder Woman's island home?
questions.fact: The island is home to the Amazons, a nation of women warriors. Older comics call it Paradise Island.

questions.question: What turned Bruce Banner into the Hulk?
questions.fact: In the 1970s TV series "The Incredible Hulk", Banner's first name was changed from Bruce to David.

questions.question: What metal is Captain America's round shield made of?
questions.fact: In Marvel stories most of the world's vibranium comes from Wakanda, Black Panther's hidden African kingdom.

questions.question: What was the name of the original Captain America?
questions.fact: Created by Joe Simon and Jack Kirby, he punched Adolf Hitler on the cover of his very first comic, dated 1941.

questions.question: What is the name of Black Panther's African homeland?
questions.fact: The 2018 film "Black Panther" was the first superhero film ever nominated for the Best Picture Oscar.

questions.question: Which artist co-created Spider-Man with Stan Lee?
questions.fact: Spider-Man debuted in 1962 in Amazing Fantasy #15, the final issue of a comic that was being cancelled.

questions.question: Whose death inspires Peter Parker to become a crime-fighting hero?
questions.fact: In his first story, the line about great power and great responsibility was a narrator's caption, not spoken by Ben.

questions.question: In which city does Batman fight crime?
questions.fact: "Gotham" was an old nickname for New York, first used by the writer Washington Irving in 1807.

questions.question: Which writer was officially credited as Batman's co-creator alongside Bob Kane only in 2015?
questions.fact: Finger is said to have suggested Batman's cowl, his grey costume, the name Gotham City and the name Bruce Wayne.

questions.question: Which Batman villain was originally a psychiatrist at Arkham Asylum?
questions.fact: Harley first appeared in "Batman: The Animated Series" in 1992, and only later joined the comics.

questions.question: Which Batman villain leaves puzzles at his crime scenes?
questions.fact: His real name is usually Edward Nygma, a pun on "E. Nigma", or enigma.

questions.question: Who was the first Robin, Batman's sidekick?
questions.fact: A former circus acrobat, Dick Grayson later grew up and became the hero Nightwing.

questions.question: What is Catwoman's real name?
questions.fact: Michelle Pfeiffer, Anne Hathaway and Zoë Kravitz have all played her on the big screen.

questions.question: What is the Penguin's real name?
questions.fact: Colin Farrell played him in "The Batman" (2022) and again in his own 2024 spin-off series, "The Penguin".

questions.question: Which name does the Flash use in most modern films and TV shows?
questions.fact: Barry gained his super-speed when lightning struck a shelf of chemicals in his police lab.

questions.question: Where does Green Lantern get his powers from?
questions.fact: The ring is powered by willpower. In classic stories it famously had no effect on anything yellow.

questions.question: Which underwater kingdom does Aquaman rule?
questions.fact: Aquaman first appeared in 1941. Jason Momoa's 2018 "Aquaman" film made over a billion dollars worldwide.

questions.question: Which X-Men leader is a powerful telepath who uses a wheelchair?
questions.fact: Patrick Stewart and James McAvoy have both played Charles Xavier in the X-Men films.

questions.question: Which X-Men hero can control the weather?
questions.fact: Halle Berry played Storm in four X-Men films between 2000 and 2014.

questions.question: What metal coats Wolverine's skeleton and claws?
questions.fact: Wolverine first appeared in 1974 in "The Incredible Hulk" comics, fighting the Hulk himself.

questions.question: What is the name of Thor's mischievous adopted brother in Marvel?
questions.fact: Tom Hiddleston originally auditioned to play Thor before being cast as Loki.

questions.question: Which villain snaps his fingers to wipe out half of all life in "Avengers: Infinity War"?
questions.fact: His creator, Jim Starlin, reportedly based the name on Thanatos, the Greek personification of death.

questions.question: Which film overtook "Avatar" in 2019 to become the highest-grossing film ever, for a while?
questions.fact: "Avatar" won back the record in 2021, after a re-release in cinemas in China.

questions.question: Which actress played Black Widow in the Marvel films?
questions.fact: In the comics, Natasha Romanoff first appeared in 1964 as a Soviet spy fighting against Iron Man.

questions.question: What was Stan Lee's real name?
questions.fact: He reportedly chose a pen name because he hoped to save his real name for a serious novel one day.

questions.question: What was Marvel Comics' original company name, in 1939?
questions.fact: Its first title, Marvel Comics #1, introduced the Human Torch and Namor the Sub-Mariner.

questions.question: What does "DC" stand for in DC Comics?
questions.fact: Batman made his debut in Detective Comics #27 in 1939, the title that gave the company its name.

questions.question: Which Fantastic Four member can stretch his body like rubber?
questions.fact: He's the scientist Reed Richards. The team's 1961 debut, by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby, launched modern Marvel.

questions.question: Which Fantastic Four member shouts "It's clobberin' time!"?
questions.fact: The Thing is pilot Ben Grimm, whose body was turned into orange rock by cosmic rays.

questions.question: What was Doctor Strange's job before he learned magic?
questions.fact: A car crash wrecked Stephen Strange's hands, sending him to the Himalayas in search of a cure.

questions.question: Which actor plays Ant-Man in the Marvel films?
questions.fact: Rudd plays Scott Lang. The original comic-book Ant-Man, Hank Pym, is played by Michael Douglas.

questions.question: Daredevil is blind. What is his day job?
questions.fact: Matt Murdock lost his sight to radioactive chemicals as a boy, which sharpened all his other senses.

questions.question: What is Venom?
questions.fact: The black suit first bonded with Spider-Man himself. Tom Hardy played Venom in three films, from 2018 to 2024.

questions.question: What is the name of Tintin's little white dog?
questions.fact: In the original French he's called Milou, reportedly after Hergé's first girlfriend.

questions.question: Which Belgian artist created Tintin?
questions.fact: Hergé is a pen name: it's the French pronunciation of R.G., the reversed initials of Georges Remi.

questions.question: What is Tintin's job?
questions.fact: Despite being a reporter, Tintin is almost never shown actually writing an article.

questions.question: What is Captain Haddock's favourite drink in Tintin?
questions.fact: The captain is famous for colourful outbursts such as "Billions of blistering blue barnacles!"

questions.question: Who brews the magic potion in "Asterix"?
questions.fact: In the Spanish and French versions, the druid is called Panoramix.

questions.question: Why is Obelix permanently super-strong?
options: He fell into the magic potion
questions.fact: Because of his fall as a baby, the druid refuses to give him any more potion, much to his annoyance.

questions.question: Asterix was created by writer René Goscinny and which artist?
questions.fact: Asterix first appeared in 1959, in the first issue of the French comic magazine Pilote.

questions.question: What is the name of Obelix's little dog in English?
questions.fact: In French he's Idéfix and in Spanish Ideafix, a pun on "idée fixe", meaning a fixed idea or obsession.

questions.question: Who created the Spanish comic "Mortadelo y Filemón"?
questions.fact: Ibáñez first drew the bumbling pair in 1958 and kept drawing them for over 60 years, until his death in 2023.

questions.question: What do Mortadelo and Filemón work as?
questions.fact: Their agency, the T.I.A., parodies the CIA. Fittingly, "tía" also means "aunt" in Spanish.

questions.question: Which comic-book cowboy "shoots faster than his own shadow"?
questions.fact: In 1983 he swapped his cigarette for a piece of straw, a change later praised by the World Health Organization.

questions.question: Who are Zipi y Zape in the classic Spanish comic?
questions.fact: Josep Escobar created the mischievous twins in 1948. "Zipizape" is a Spanish word for a scuffle or commotion.

questions.question: Who played Batman in the 2022 film "The Batman"?
questions.fact: Before Batman, Pattinson was best known as the vampire Edward Cullen in the "Twilight" films.

questions.question: Which magic word turns young Billy Batson into a superhero?
questions.fact: Each letter stands for a hero or god: Solomon, Hercules, Atlas, Zeus, Achilles and Mercury.

questions.question: Comic artist Jack Kirby is often nicknamed…
questions.fact: Kirby co-created Captain America, the Fantastic Four, the Hulk and the X-Men.

questions.question: Who wrote the graphic novel "Watchmen"?
questions.fact: It was the only graphic novel on Time magazine's 2005 list of the 100 best English-language novels since 1923.

questions.question: Who is the teenage hero of the animated film "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse" (2018)?
questions.fact: The film won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature, beating Pixar's "Incredibles 2".

questions.question: What is the name of S.H.I.E.L.D.'s eyepatch-wearing director?
questions.fact: In the early 2000s Marvel's "Ultimate" comics redrew Fury to look like Samuel L. Jackson, years before he played him.

questions.question: Who is Peter Parker's newspaper boss at the Daily Bugle?
questions.fact: J.K. Simmons played him in 2002's "Spider-Man" and returned to the role in 2019's "Far From Home".

questions.question: Which girlfriend of Peter Parker died in a famous 1973 comic?
questions.fact: Her death, at the hands of the Green Goblin, is often said to mark the end of comics' "Silver Age".

questions.question: Which superhero team includes Cyclops, Jean Grey and Beast?
questions.fact: Stan Lee and Jack Kirby created the X-Men in 1963 as mutants, people born with their powers.
